title: Tenant quarantine + region fallthrough: graceful degradation for Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped quarantine mechanism and region-fallthrough policy to keep Dedicated and Private deployments available during region outages or noisy tenants, while preserving SLOs for unaffected tenants. Scope covers control-plane isolation primitives, tenant-level circuit breakers, region-aware routing fallback, and load-shedding policies that can trigger soft-degrades (reduced token budgets / lower-quality model variants) or hard-rejects. This ticket covers design, prototype, e2e tests, monitoring hooks, and rollout plan for runtime-1.19.

Background: Recent smoke tests and a minor multi-tenant outage showed a single misbehaving tenant during a rolling upgrade can cause head-of-line blocking in the control plane and increase tail latency for other tenants in the same Dedicated pool. Private/VPC customers have less tolerance for cross-tenant interference. We need a resilient mechanism that: 1) isolates noisy tenants quickly, 2) reroutes traffic to healthy regions where appropriate, and 3) provides safe automated behaviors during upgrades to prevent cascading failures.

Design highlights and decisions: 
- Tenant quarantine: control-plane maintains a tenant health state machine (HEALTHY / DEGRADED / QUARANTINED). Quarantine is initiated by circuit-breaker rules (error rate, p95/p99 latency thresholds, token consumption anomalies). Quarantined tenants are rate-limited and optionally served only from dedicated fallback capacity or low-cost model variants.
- Multi-region fallthrough: requests for quarantined or capacity-limited tenants can be routed to a secondary region when allowed by customer config (default: opt-in for Private, opt-out for Hosted). Fallthrough respects data residency and KMS constraints; routing logic consults tenant metadata and the routing policy store.
- Circuit breakers: two-layer breakers — per-connection/runtime-sidebreaker and per-tenant/global-circuit. Per-tenant circuit-breaker aggregates across nodes in a pool. Breaker state is persisted to the distributed store with TTL to avoid flapping.
- Load shedding policy: soft degrade path (reduce max tokens, switch to quantized/cheaper model variants, disable streaming) versus hard reject. Policy is configurable per-tenant and by customer tier.
- Upgrade safety: introduce staged rollouts by tenant risk profile (low-risk tenants first), and preflight checks that detect elevated error/latency rates before advancing phase. Upgrades can auto-pause and trigger quarantines for affected tenants to prevent noisy rollback ripples.

Trade-offs: 
- Complexity vs observability: adding tenant state and per-tenant routing increases control plane metadata cardinality and write load. We mitigate by sharding tenant metadata and using TTLs and bulk state compaction.
- Latency vs isolation: per-tenant checks add microsecond overhead; optimized fast-path caches for HEALTHY tenants will minimize impact.
- Data residency constraints limit automated fallthrough for some customers. For those, we default to local soft-degrades instead of cross-region routing.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Design doc reviewed and approved by Reliability and Security.
- Prototype that demonstrates quarantining a noisy tenant in a Dedicated pool and verifying other tenants maintain p99 latency within SLO during the incident.
- Automated integration test that simulates region outage and verifies configured fallthrough/RPO behavior.
- Console shows tenant quarantine state, reason, and suggested remediation; alerting triggers for quarantine events.
- Rollout plan with canary groups and automatic rollback triggers implemented in runtime-1.19 release pipeline.

Runbook / Observability: telemetry must include per-tenant error-rate, token burn rate, active connections, last-quarantine-reason, and region-fallthrough events. Dashboards for oncall to triage quarantines and a playbook for when to escalate to product/security.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc linked and approved by Reliability & Security
Prototype isolates noisy tenant without SLO regressions for others in Dedicated pool (measured p95/p99)
Integration test covers single-region failure and verifies regional fallthrough respects data residency settings
Console UI exposes tenant state and allows manual quarantine/unquarantine with audit log entries
Canary rollout plan implemented with automated pause/rollback on elevated error/latency signals
comments: 2026-02-13 - Aisha N. Patel: Initial triage and problem statement. Spoke with Support about two incidents in Jan where noisy tenants caused 3x p99 increase in pool. Raised requirement to protect Private customers from cross-tenant interference.

2026-02-20 - Marco L. Ortega: Prototype started. Implemented in-memory per-node breaker and a basic sharded tenant-state store. Observed ~4% CPU overhead in microbench; added fast-path cache for HEALTHY tenants to target <1% overhead.

2026-02-27 - Reliability review: Decided to persist breaker state to distributed store (etcd-backed) with TTL to avoid flapping. Security notes: cross-region fallthrough must not be default for Private customers due to KMS/data residency; updated design accordingly.

2026-03-04 - QA: Created an integration test that simulates a tenant producing high error rate for 2 minutes. Test asserts other tenants maintain p99 within existing SLO. Found an issue where circuit state didn't compact; added compaction job to background worker.
2026-03-09 - Marco L. Ortega: Console PR opened for quarantine visibility and manual override. Linked PR and added unit tests for audit log entries. Preparing canary config (10 low-risk tenants).

2026-03-12 - Oncall run: Ran chaos test in staging causing a region failover. Observed one customer with strict data residency failed to fallthrough (expected) and was soft-degraded; dashboard alerting fired and runbook flow executed successfully. Marking milestone: staging validation complete.
